AUDIT QUESTION: DEC-1 follow-up to late Heimdall findings. (1) The G9 row is split: G9_tail is now the calibrated gate result alone; a new row outro_locked is FAIL on an outro conform fallback. Before, the same condition was hidden inside G9 as (identical or not fallback), and identical already contained 'and not fallback', so the term was 'not fallback'. Verify there is no acceptance change: the run must still HOLD on a conform fallback and on a luma failure (verdict_for holds on any FAIL row), and nothing else changed. (2) Tests: TestTailRows; the G9 must-fail assertion checks the boolean strictly and the measured luma against the floor constant; sys.path gains the pipeline dir (no module name is shared with segment_v1). Find any way this loosens acceptance or any test that passes vacuously. Only state what you can verify from the diff; if uncertain, say so. (this chunk: pipeline/run_fresh.py)

+    """G9_tail is the DEC-1 calibrated gate alone (no exception path). outro_locked: the luma floor is
+    the approved reference's LOCKED outro tail, so a conform fallback (some other outro) fails closed
+    on its own row even when its tail clears the floor (Heimdall DEC-1 audit: keep the two apart)."""
+    return {"G9_tail": _status(g9_pass), "outro_locked": _status(not conform_fallback)}
+
+
 def stage_gates(run, final16, man16, final9, man9):
     # Keep the source-relative sharpness threshold local to this stage so QA does not
     # depend on module-global lookup state during long production runs. Threshold unchanged.

     adj = L.Adjudicator()
